Three individuals have pleaded guilty to defrauding Maryland’s Medicaid program of more than $3.6 million through fake mental health service claims. Our office will continue holding those accountable who steal from programs meant to support Marylanders in need.

Full press release: https://t.co/nbK1NoIH7b

A former D.C. teacher has pleaded guilty to felony theft and insurance fraud after stealing over $430,000 through false insurance claims.

Our office secured full restitution for the money stolen from the American Family Life Assurance Company of Columbus (AFLAC) and National Teachers Association Life Insurance. Fraud like this drives up costs for everyone—and we’re holding those who abuse the system accountable.

Full release: https://t.co/NDZ3PhsKtl

Zak Shirley, Director of our Medicaid Fraud & Vulnerable Victims Unit, will speak at the #PROTECTWeek2025 press conference with @AARPMD 

In honor of World Elder Abuse Awareness Day yesterday, we’re reaffirming our commitment to protecting older Marylanders from abuse, neglect, and exploitation.

🔴 Tune in live Now: https://t.co/HvIGF43QEI

A St. Mary’s County woman has been sentenced for defrauding Medicaid out of thousands of dollars by billing for in-home care she never provided. She is now banned from providing care to vulnerable adults and from participating in publicly funded healthcare programs.
 
My office will continue holding accountable those who exploit programs meant to serve Marylanders in need.
 
Full press release: https://t.co/KepLv6IuYU

The federal government is handing over personal Medicaid data to immigration enforcement — a move that puts millions of people’s privacy at risk. This could stop Maryland families, including pregnant people and children, from getting the care they’re legally entitled to. We’re taking legal action as part of a multistate coalition to stop this harmful policy and protect access to healthcare.

Full press release: https://t.co/Naul2BBlXu

Congratulations to OAG attorneys Zak Shirley and Alisa Bralove-Scherr on receiving Outstanding Capstone Awards from the Maryland Certified Public Manager Program!

Zak, Director of our Medicaid Fraud & Vulnerable Victims Unit, proposed a new model to combat institutional neglect in long-term care, an approach that contributed to a $1.28 million settlement and lasting oversight reforms.

Alisa, Attorney-Mediator with the Public Access Ombudsman, developed a training process to better equip mediation volunteers in our Consumer Protection Division—boosting effectiveness, engagement, and retention.

We're proud to recognize their leadership and innovation in public service!

The Trump administration is pushing a new rule that could cause up to 1.8 million people including 34,000 Marylanders—to lose their health insurance. It threatens to raise premiums, increase out-of-pocket costs, and exclude coverage for gender-affirming care.

I joined a multistate lawsuit to stop it. Marylanders shouldn’t have to choose between rent and lifesaving treatment.

Full press release: https://t.co/3TYvbmbRqO

My Statement on the Trump Administration’s Unprecedented Move to Allow ICE to Access Medicaid Database:

“This agreement is a grave breach of the public’s trust and a direct threat to the privacy and safety of families across our state. It undermines the core purpose of our healthcare system by turning it into a tool of surveillance rather than a source of care. By compromising the confidentiality between patients and providers, the federal government is jeopardizing the privacy of Medicaid recipients and placing immigrant families in an impossible position: choose between critical medical treatment or the risk of being swept into immigration enforcement.

This reckless policy will deter people from seeking routine and urgent care, leading to worse health outcomes and placing an unsustainable burden on our hospitals and clinics when preventable conditions become emergencies. We will use every legal tool available to safeguard the personal medical information of our residents and uphold the integrity of our healthcare system. This is not only unlawful—it is a deeply harmful act that will separate families, sow fear in our communities, and put lives at risk.”

Today I announced new criminal charges against a former insurance agent accused of obstruction of justice and fabricating evidence. This marks the fourth time he has been charged since last fall.
The defendant allegedly created a fake document and altered a client’s signature to use in court. He is also facing multiple cases for stealing from clients and continuing to sell insurance after his license was revoked.

My Office will continue to hold financial professionals accountable when they exploit the trust of Marylanders.

Full press release: https://t.co/SfojYzjugY

Today we joined 23 states in suing the Trump administration for cutting off Medicaid funding to Planned Parenthood—putting essential healthcare at risk for more than 1 million patients nationwide.

Planned Parenthood provides vital services like cancer screenings, STI testing, and wellness exams—care many people can’t get anywhere else. We’re fighting to keep that care accessible in Maryland and nationwide.

Full press release: https://t.co/eUWUUdU9i2

We’ve joined a lawsuit to stop the Trump administration from trying to block healthcare providers from offering legal, medically necessary care to transgender, intersex, and nonbinary individuals.
 
In some states, these efforts are already leading some clinics to cancel appointments or limit services — leaving young people without the care they need. This lawsuit defends families’ right to access safe, legal healthcare without interference.
 
Full press release: https://t.co/T0mXDKQltr

Illegal offshore gaming operations are putting Marylanders at risk of losing their livelihoods and the money they need to pay for housing and essentials like food or healthcare—especially young people and vulnerable adults, and costing states billions in lost tax revenue.

I joined 50 attorneys general in calling on the U.S. Department of Justice to take stronger action against these dangerous, unregulated platforms that operate outside the law and without consumer protections.

Full press release: https://t.co/4ALRSSxAak

It was an honor for our Medicaid Fraud and Vulnerable Victims Unit (MFVVU) to join the Baltimore City State’s Attorney’s Office at today’s Third Annual Older Adult Luncheon. Protecting older Marylanders is a responsibility we all share—and today was about making sure they know where to find help if they or their loved ones face abuse, neglect, or financial exploitation.

🔗 Learn more about how our MFVVU carries out this work: https://t.co/Mgs551IoOd

Thank you to the State’s Attorney’s Office for bringing so many partners and community resources together under one roof.

#ElderJustice #OlderAdults #ElderAbusePrevention

Why I Serve: Lisa Marts

Guided by a lifelong commitment to care for others, Lisa Marts began her career as a prosecutor before bringing her talents here to the Maryland Office of the Attorney General.

As Deputy Director of our Medicaid Fraud & Vulnerable Victims Unit, she works tirelessly to protect older Marylanders, improve nursing home conditions, and hold abusers accountable.

My Office’s Medicaid Fraud and Vulnerable Victims Unit reached a $200,000 settlement with Patapsco Healthcare for providing substandard care to residents. Our investigation uncovered serious failures — from poor wound care and unsafe conditions to preventable overdoses.

Under the settlement, Patapsco must fund a quality improvement plan and will be monitored for four years to ensure residents receive the safe, dignified care they deserve.

Full press release: https://t.co/DtKnCYh2dc

Scam Alert: Fake health insurance sites could target Marylanders during Open Enrollment.

✅ Only shop at https://t.co/c9RPDUjAE2, the official site (check for “.gov”)

💳 If someone asks you to pay for help enrolling, it’s a scam.
Stay safe and verify before you share your information.

🔗 Read more: https://t.co/pIcDRZAwHU

Today, along with 21 other Attorneys General and the Governor of Pennsylvania, our Office secured a preliminary injunction blocking the Trump Administration from enforcing a new statutory provision that would strip Medicaid funding from Planned Parenthood and other essential health centers.

Full Release: https://t.co/kKNevqkNdZ

Last week, a Baltimore County jury found a former insurance agent guilty of misappropriating $36,500 from a client and then trying to cover it up by writing a fake letter and pasting the client’s signature onto it to make it look like he approved the payment.

Marylanders deserve financial advisors they can trust, and we will hold anyone who abuses that trust accountable.

Full press release: https://t.co/5BNG4lSjEm

When a nursing home fails to meet basic care standards, vulnerable Marylanders suffer preventable harm. Today I announced a $400,000 settlement with Orchard Hill Rehabilitation and Healthcare Center that mandates real reforms and ongoing oversight so residents receive the safe, dignified care they deserve.

This settlement holds Orchard Hill accountable and requires meaningful changes to protect those entrusted to their care.

Full press release: https://t.co/fof3PF8ta9

A Parkville mother and daughter were sentenced for defrauding Maryland Medicaid of more than $3.6 million by billing for mental health services that were never provided. 

The mother received a 10-year prison sentence, and her daughter was placed on probation and ordered to pay restitution.

Full press release: https://t.co/PniOUYSWRf
